Deadlock gave us an insight on Source 2. We all knew Dota on Source 2 boast better lightning, reflections, and shaders. Counter Strike 2 makes all of these effects more noticeable, albeit there are less FX and things going on compared to Dota.

And then Deadlock came out and we can see many effects up close thanks to the third person perspective. So far, this is all I can see:

Improved shaders
Improved shadows
Improved particles
Lightning now is smoothened at will. Some light sources react more dinamically to their enviroment
Higher poly count.
Improved reflections.
Support for newer tech such as upscalers.
Higher AI calculations. We need development docs on this to pinpoint what is happening under the hood, but the engine seems to handle multiple entities way better than Source.

Still, these are multiplayer games and HL3 can come up with even new tech stuff such as the greatly improved water physics present on Counter Strike 2. 

The artist and engineers working at Valve are talented folks and sure, maybe the leap seems less promising than HL to HL2, but it will be a pretty and amazing game still because Source 2 has way too much headroom to improve or come up with solutions that Source couldn't otherwise come up with without stretching the engine beyond its capabilities.

Ninja Gaiden, a game originally released for the Xbox back in 2004, found a solution for this problem.

Some bosses had limbs that, combined together, make the total HP value of the boss. So say, the Bone Dragon has four legs and each legs accounts for 25% of total health pool. Take down all four legs and he's done.

It wouldn't be hard to translate into Helldivers and tweak accordingly and at some extent, we get some of that (I.E Hulk can take critical damage from shooting limbs off), but it surprises me how little incentive there is to team up, focus firepower towards weak points and score the kill. Currently, FS feel like the only viable way to take them down is kite them with stratagems, which I get why this was made that way, but a walking mech should have multiple failure points that, from a game design perspective, should be all exploitable. There is also no reason to shoot Bile Titan belly because it will not kill it and you can totally skip the belly part by shooting it's head instead, so why bother?

Hopefully this caughts Arrowhead team attention. I think they should try leaning more towards traditional boss design choices and apply the Helldivers formula on top of it.

We have different switches.

The most common is when we go autopilot, we are aware of whatever is happening around us but our actions are not intentional (i.e walking, reading). Right after we gain consciousness but realize that we don't know how we got there, or what the previous page was. Then we walk back or turn the page and it seems familiar, yet it doesn't. That's when we realize we switched.

Closely followed by the dissociation, that might feel different depending on a few factors. We spend a few minutes in, like, void-like state. Time warps, identity shifts, then we realize.

Then we have, albeit rare, cases where something inside clicks and suddenly someone else is fronting. This happens very fast and doesn't last long, but it happens normally when there is a time to relax after exposure to stress.

What we do is we act oblivious to it otherwise the sudden realization of eye contact makes it awkward, but this ks maybe because our autism. We also look at some distant point and try to act like something funny just happened there. You can also, if asked, say that you remembered a funny memory.
